memories.content: The user's mother's birthday falls in the third week of January.
At the user's last family meal out, noise from the next table made conversation nearly impossible.
At a barbecue at home in the same month, the user was comfortable because no one had to raise their voice.
During their mother's birthday meal, the user left a restaurant with loud music after 30 minutes.
When discussing postponed matters with family, the user prefers a quiet, one-on-one dining environment.
At a large banquet hall reserved by their older sister, the user remembered the surrounding noise more than the food.
On a day the user ate grilled food at home with their younger brother, conversation was easy to continue, so the user stayed another hour after the meal.
The user's mother considers having the whole family eat at the same time more important than receiving a birthday gift.

When proposing a birthday meal for the user's mother, check the schedule and attendees; if conversation is the purpose, first consider a low-noise location, then confirm the final choice with the user.
The local agent can compare past dining environments and the user's responses, but those records alone cannot determine the location of the next gathering.
The user recorded a family dinner in the calendar for the final week of November.
In a crowded restaurant, the user had to ask several times for orders to be repeated, interrupting the flow of conversation.
When the user held the next gathering at their father's home, they continued the conversation on the sofa after the meal.
At a gathering with loud music prepared by their older sister, the user developed a headache and went outside briefly.
On a day the user held a yard barbecue with their younger brother, the open space dispersed the sound and made conversation easier.
After seeing a message that their maternal aunt would arrive at 5 p.m., the user delayed meal preparation by an hour.
On a day the user waited without knowing their maternal uncle's arrival time, they reheated the food twice.
The user's maternal uncle considers it easier to time his departure when he knows the family meal's start time in advance.
Before scheduling a family meal, confirm the attendees' arrival times and the location with the user.
Available restaurant reservation times may diminish quickly during the year-end gathering season.

analysis.overview: The frames consistently favor conversation-friendly family settings and coordinated timing, while contributing different event dates and planning details. Their guidance is complementary: maternal birthday planning gives conditional priority to low noise, whereas general family-meal planning emphasizes arrival times and location confirmation.

relations.reason: The memories describe different experiences and preferences, but they consistently inform the same venue-selection consideration without contradiction.
relations.summary: Across both frames, the user’s family conversations and comfort fare worse in loud or crowded dining settings and better in quieter or home-based settings.

relations.reason: The mother’s preference and the compared frame’s timing experiences provide complementary reasons to coordinate attendees and meal times.
relations.summary: Coordinating family-meal timing matters because simultaneous attendance is valued and arrival or start-time information affects preparation and individual planning.

relations.reason: The guidance is compatible, but its distinct occasion and purpose conditions must be preserved rather than treated as identical.
relations.summary: Both frames require user-confirmed family-meal planning, with maternal birthday meals conditionally prioritizing low noise for conversation and general family meals specifically requiring arrival-time confirmation.

relations.reason: One memory limits what historical evidence can determine, while the other supplies a current seasonal constraint relevant to the same location decision.
relations.summary: Choosing a gathering location requires more than past dining-response records and may also depend on rapidly changing restaurant availability during the year-end season.
